vulnerabilities.description: XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus command-line tools. Prior to version 5.8.3, if lzma_index_decoder() was used to decode an Index that contained no Records, the resulting lzma_index was left in a state where a subsequent lzma_index_append() would allocate too little memory, and a buffer overflow would occur. This issue has been patched in version 5.8.3.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not use liblzma at runtime.

ratings.justification: liblzma5 is present only for OS package tooling in the Ubuntu base layer. No Liquibase Secure component loads it.

analysis.detail: XZ Utils liblzma heap buffer overflow when lzma_index_append() is called on an index produced by lzma_index_decoder() from an Index with no Records. Liquibase Secure inherits liblzma5 from the Ubuntu base image, where dpkg-deb, apt and libsystemd link it. The Liquibase CLI runs on the JVM, which does not link liblzma. The container entrypoint invokes no xz-capable tool. The Liquibase release archive is a gzip tarball, so the image build does not use liblzma to unpack it either. A source review found no references to liblzma or xz in Liquibase Secure. Ubuntu has published fixed packages (5.6.1+really5.4.5-1ubuntu0.3 for 24.04, 5.2.5-2ubuntu1.1 for 22.04, USN-8362-1); image builds from 5.2.1 onward carry the fix.
